Learn indirect control: scout with a flag, supply your colony, and direct an attack.
Start introduction
Your globules act on their own. You choose their jobs through buildings and flags. In this short introduction, scout a landmark, expand food supply, grow your workforce, and direct a small attack.
Allow about 10 minutes. You can save from the game menu and resume through Load game. Normal hunger and combat rules apply. Choose Tutorial lessons from the main menu to practice more skills.
Your choice could not be saved. You can continue playing; this recommendation may appear again next time.

Build another Inn
Supply your new Inn
Grow the workforce

Open Flags and place an Exploration Flag over the stone patch east of your colony. Assign one explorer. Watch it travel to the flag.
Open Build and place an Inn near wheat. Assign available workers to construct it. Leave your existing Inn supplied.
Select your finished new Inn and give it at least one supplier. Wait for a worker to deliver wheat.
Select the Swarm. Set its worker target to at least 2, and its production ratios to workers only. Keep both Inns supplied while a new worker is born.
Find the enemy Swarm farther east. Use a War Flag to direct your warriors against it. Help is available if you need a reminder.
Help / why?

Use the minimap to move the view east and find the stone patch. Choose Exploration Flag in Flags, place it on the stone, then leave placement with the secondary mouse button. Select the flag and request 1 explorer. Flags request units; they do not move them instantly. Explorers may stop to eat.

Construction consumes wood delivered by workers. Choose Inn from the building controls (the building palette), place it in clear ground near wheat, and request 2 builders. A worker target is a request, not a count of workers already present. Keep suppliers at your existing Inn and Swarm. Any valid location counts.

Construction and everyday supply have separate worker targets. Select the finished Inn and increase its operating target. A supplier gathers wheat and carries it here. Hungry globules eat at Inns; a building with no suppliers will eventually run out. Keep the wheat patch accessible.

The Swarm consumes wheat to produce units. Set worker production to 1 and explorer and warrior production to 0. Increase the Swarm worker target to 2 or more. More suppliers can deliver wheat faster, but they compete with other jobs. Maintain food supply at both Inns.

Open Flags, choose War Flag, and place it over the enemy Swarm east of the stone. Select the flag and request up to 4 warriors. A small radius keeps them concentrated. Leave placement with the secondary mouse button before selecting the flag. If no warriors remain, produce more at the Swarm. Warriors may stop to eat; keep the Inns supplied.
Your explorer needs an assigned Exploration Flag at the eastern stone patch. Check its target and explorer count.

If you removed the new Inn, build another. Otherwise check the construction site and its worker target. Existing supply jobs may occupy your workers; keep food running while making builders available.
Select the finished new Inn. Check its worker target and watch for wheat deliveries. Workers may need time to travel or eat.

Check your War Flag, requested warrior count, and food supply. Your warriors need time to travel and attack.

removed.source: Tutorial ▸

Welcome to Globulation 2! This tutorial teaches colony management over four missions. You can save your progress from the game menu and load it later from the main menu. Press Space to continue, or tap OK on a touch screen. Some messages disappear after you continue; use Message history to read them again.
You begin with a Swarm and one worker. Let's see how they work together.
Your worker harvests wheat and carries it to the Swarm. The Swarm uses wheat to produce new units, making it essential to your colony.
Select your globule, the moving unit, with a left-click or a tap.
The unit information shows its food level falling over time. Your globule is getting hungry. When food bars are visible, the blue bar beneath the unit shows its remaining food.
Globules eat at Inns. Clear the selection with a right-click, or tap empty ground on a touch screen.

Open the building controls, choose Inn, and place it near wheat. Follow your worker's harvesting route if you cannot spot the wheat. On touch screens, use Build and confirm a valid placement. When finished, leave placement mode with a right-click or the touch Cancel control.
Good! The Inn's building site is in place.
A worker from the Swarm can now build the Inn. The worker gathers wood from nearby trees and brings it to the site. Wait for construction to finish.
The finished Inn needs wheat. An assigned worker will gather it, just as a worker supplies the Swarm.
The Inn's yellow resource bar rises as wheat arrives. It shows how much wheat the Inn has in stock.
Now let's learn how to assign work.
One worker supplies the Swarm and another supplies the Inn. Either may pause to eat at the Inn. That is normal.

Select the Swarm and find its worker assignment control. On desktop it is labeled Working; on touch screens, use the assigned workers and target control. The target is how many workers you want at this building.
Use the assignment control to set the Swarm's worker target to 0. Then select the Inn and set its target to 0 too.
Your workers are now idle, but they still need food. An Inn with no assigned workers will eventually run out of wheat.
A globule that cannot find food will lose health and may die. A Hospital can heal damaged globules, but you must also keep the Inns supplied.
Build a Hospital using the building controls. It does not need wheat, so place it near wood or in a central spot near your Swarm.
Select the Hospital's building site and set its worker target to 2. Two workers can finish it faster.
The Hospital is ready. Injured globules can now visit it to recover their health.
The black areas are unexplored. Units reveal nearby ground as they move. Workers follow their jobs, so they are hard to use for scouting. Explorers are designed for that task.
Select the Swarm and find the production ratios for workers, explorers, and warriors. Increase the explorer ratio to 1.
With worker and explorer ratios both at 1, the Swarm produces equal numbers of each over time. Set the worker ratio to 0 so it produces only explorers for now.
Set the Swarm's worker assignment target back to 1 so a worker can bring it wheat.
Select the Inn and set its worker target to 1 too. Your growing colony needs a steady food supply.
Now wait for the Swarm to produce an explorer.
Your explorer flies around the colony, revealing more ground. Let the Swarm produce a second explorer before continuing.
Select the Swarm again. Set the explorer production ratio to 0 and the worker ratio to 1 to resume producing workers.
There is stone east of your base. Remember this location; you will need stone later.
The trees south of the stone are orange trees. Select them to see their resource information. We will return to fruit later; for now, focus on the Swarm.
Set your Swarm to produce workers only: worker ratio 1, explorer and warrior ratios 0.
Let's grow the colony faster. Select the Swarm and set its worker assignment target to 6. You may not have six workers yet; new workers can fill the extra jobs as they become available.
We will start the next tasks when you have 8 workers. Keep the Swarm and Inn supplied while the population grows.
Several workers are now supplying the Swarm. More wheat deliveries mean it can produce units more quickly.
A new worker costs 5 wheat. Carrying wheat from a distant field takes time, so a Swarm often needs more suppliers than an Inn. Place food-dependent buildings near wheat when possible.
You now have at least 8 workers. Select the Swarm and reduce its worker assignment target to 1 to slow population growth while we build.
Your colony needs more feeding capacity. Build a second Inn north of the existing one.
Assign free workers to the new Inn's construction site. It needs only 3 wood, so more than 3 builders will not help much.
The finished Inn returns to its operating worker target, normally 1. Construction and everyday supply use separate assignment targets.
Workers can learn to move faster. A Racetrack provides that training.
Open the building controls and find Racetrack. On desktop, hover over its icon to inspect its description and cost. On touch screens, select it in Build to prepare placement. Do not place it yet.
A Racetrack needs plenty of wood and a little stone. Choose a central location so units can reach it easily.
Build a Racetrack, perhaps south of the Swarm. Leave clear space around it: training buildings need room to expand when upgraded.
Set the Racetrack construction site's worker target between 5 and 7. It needs 7 construction materials in total.
Once finished, a Racetrack trains visiting units without a continuing supply of construction materials or wheat.
Globules are entering the Racetrack to train. Once trained, they can run faster.
Select the Racetrack to inspect training progress. Its progress indicators show how close the units inside are to finishing.
Your trained workers travel faster and can deliver resources sooner. Keep watching food stocks as the colony grows; faster deliveries help only if enough Inns remain supplied.

Find the worker population counter in the HUD. The total shows your population; the available-worker figure helps you spot spare workers or unfilled jobs. Use free workers without assigning more jobs than the colony can support.
The HUD also shows explorer and warrior counts. Check these when planning production or assigning units to flags.
You have 2 Inns. Each basic Inn can feed 4 units at once, so together they have 8 feeding places. More than 8 units can become hungry, so leave enough capacity for queues.
Two Inns will not support a growing colony forever. Build extra feeding capacity before shortages turn into starvation.
Build 3 more Inns near wheat. Hungry workers stop working, and prolonged starvation kills them. Assign available workers to construction while keeping your existing food supply running.
Finish building 3 more Inns, bringing your total to 5.
The new Inns use their operating assignment targets after construction, normally 1 worker each. Check that they have suppliers and enough wheat.
The Racetrack has improved travel on land. Now let's teach the colony to swim.

A Swimming Pool teaches units to swim and needs wood to build. Place one in the large clearing northeast of the base, north of the stone. Leave space around it for upgrades and resource growth, and assign available workers to construction.

A Swimming Pool teaches units to swim and needs wood to build. Place one in the large clearing northeast of the base, north of the stone. Leave space around it for upgrades and resource growth, and assign available workers to construction.
The Swimming Pool is ready. Globules can now enter and learn to swim.
Select the Swimming Pool to inspect training progress. A basic Pool trains 2 globules at a time, just like a basic Racetrack.
Your trained globules can now swim. Soon we will give them a job that requires crossing water.
There is more to learn. If you need a break, save your progress from the game menu and return later.
Your colony has food and physical training. A School will teach workers the skills needed for better buildings.
A School improves workers' harvesting and construction skills. Building one requires algae, which grows in water. Your swimming workers can gather it.
Protect important training buildings. A School does not have to stand beside water; a sheltered inland location can keep it safer from attack.
Build a School in a protected spot, such as behind the Swimming Pool or southwest of the Swarm beside the Racetrack. Assign available workers to build it.

Select a building to see the workers assigned to it. On desktop, the configurable Toggle draw unit paths action can also show lines from units to their destinations; see Settings, Controls for its current shortcut. Wait for the School to finish.
Your colony now has Inns, a Hospital, a Racetrack, a Swimming Pool, and a School. It is time to prepare its defenses.
We have not produced any warriors yet. Without them, the colony has little protection against an attack.
Select the Swarm and set the warrior production ratio to 2. Leave the worker ratio at 1 so the colony keeps producing workers too.
The Swarm will now produce roughly 2 warriors for every worker. Assign more workers to supply it if you want faster production.
Your first warrior is ready and will begin training. Wait for a second warrior before continuing.
Warriors use the Racetrack and Swimming Pool too. They can also train their attack skills at Barracks.

Barracks improve attack strength and attack speed. Strength increases damage per hit; speed increases how often a warrior attacks. Well-trained warriors can defeat much larger groups of untrained enemies.
Build Barracks near wood, which is needed for construction.
Assign available workers to the Barracks building site. Keep enough workers on food supply and avoid creating more jobs than they can fill.
The Barracks are ready. Warriors can now train their attack skills there.
Our colony can grow stronger by upgrading its buildings.
Workers trained at the School can construct upgrades. Select an eligible building and look for Upgrade in its building controls. Damaged buildings may need Repair first.
Let's decide what to upgrade first. Our Inns still have spare capacity, so they can wait.
The Hospital also has room. We can focus on the School, Racetrack, Swimming Pool, or Barracks.
Upgrade the Racetrack first so units can learn to move even faster.
Select the Racetrack and choose Upgrade in its building controls. Units inside must leave before construction begins, so the change may not be immediate.
Assign available workers to the Racetrack upgrade. Only workers with the required School training can build a level 2 construction site.
Wait for the Racetrack upgrade to finish. Higher-level buildings take more resources and time to construct.
Your level 2 Racetrack is complete. It occupies more ground than before, which is why we left a gap. A building cannot upgrade without enough room to expand.
Now upgrade the Barracks and the Swimming Pool to level 2. We will continue when both are finished.
Upgraded buildings can generally serve more globules or offer better training. A level 2 Inn, for example, has 7 feeding places and feeds units faster than a basic Inn.
The enemy is nearby. Let's prepare for an attack.
Towers shoot at enemies within range. Walls help protect them. We will use both to defend a narrow approach to the colony.
Place towers in pairs if space allows. Walls can protect three sides, but leave a route open so workers can deliver stone ammunition.
Look east of the Swimming Pool, north of the other fruit trees. A narrow crossing leads toward another island. This is a good place to defend.
Plan room for 2 towers between the trees and the shore. Leave access behind them for stone deliveries and space on the other sides for walls. Do not wall the workers out.
Build 2 towers there. Assign 2 or 3 workers to each construction site, depending on how many are available in the HUD counters.
Use the building controls to place wall sections around the three outward-facing sides of the towers. Keep the side toward your colony open for workers.
Each wall section creates a construction job and needs 1 stone. If workers cannot fill every job at once, they can finish the sections in turn.
Wait for both towers and several wall sections to finish. The towers also need stone ammunition; the distant quarry makes deliveries slow. Increase their worker targets if you have spare workers.
Your colony has food, training, and defenses. Buildings can advance once more to level 3, providing stronger training and greater capacity. Keep improving them as resources and worker skills allow.
Look northwest of your base for the enemy colony. Move the view there now.
Explored ground can still be hidden by fog of war. To see the enemy's current activity, we need an explorer nearby.
Open Flags. This gives you flags and zones for directing units without controlling each globule individually.
Choose the Exploration Flag, shown with a kite-shaped symbol. Flags can be placed over land, water, resources, and unexplored ground.

Place an Exploration Flag over the suspected enemy base. An approximate location is enough to start scouting. Leave placement mode with a right-click, or finish the placement using the touch controls.

The outline around the flag shows its working radius. An assigned explorer will scout that area. Check your explorer count if none arrives, and produce another at the Swarm if needed. Press Space or tap OK once the explorer reaches the area.
The enemy has many workers and a gathered army. Let's prepare our defenses before it attacks.
Open Flags and choose the blue Guard zone. Use the mode for adding ground to the zone, rather than removing it. On touch screens, choose Paint rather than Erase.
Choose a brush shape and size. The large square is useful for painting a compact defensive area.

Paint a Guard zone just behind your towers, where the enemy is likely to approach. Click or tap to paint a spot, or drag to cover more ground. On touch screens, use Pan when you need to move the view while painting.
Available warriors will move into the Guard zone. Make it large enough for the defenders but small enough to keep them concentrated at the crossing. Now wait for the attack.
The enemy is approaching the crossing!
We are under attack. Watch how your trained warriors and towers defend the position.
You survived! Now open Flags and choose the spiked War Flag. Place it over the enemy Swarm to direct an attack there.
Leave placement mode and select the War Flag. Assign more than 1 warrior, then reduce its radius to concentrate the attack around the enemy Swarm. Wait for your warriors to arrive.
The attack has begun. Your warriors must get past the enemy towers to reach its Swarm.
Your warriors have reached the enemy base. Keep the attack focused on the Swarm.
You destroyed the enemy Swarm. Congratulations! You have completed the tutorial and learned the basics of food supply, assignments, training, upgrades, scouting, and combat.

Learn indirect control: scout with a flag, supply your colony, and direct an attack.
Start introduction
Your globules act on their own. You choose their jobs through buildings and flags. In this short introduction, scout a landmark, expand food supply, grow your workforce, and direct a small attack.
Allow about 10 minutes. You can save from the game menu and resume through Load game. Normal hunger and combat rules apply. Choose Tutorial lessons from the main menu to practice more skills.

Open Flags and place an Exploration Flag over the stone patch east of your colony. Assign one explorer. Watch it travel to the flag.
Open Build and place an Inn near wheat. Assign available workers to construct it. Leave your existing Inn supplied.
Select your finished new Inn and give it at least one supplier. Wait for a worker to deliver wheat.
Select the Swarm. Set its worker target to at least 2, and its production ratios to workers only. Keep both Inns supplied while a new worker is born.
Find the enemy Swarm farther east. Use a War Flag to direct your warriors against it. Help is available if you need a reminder.
Help / why?

Use the minimap to move the view east and find the stone patch. Choose Exploration Flag in Flags, place it on the stone, then leave placement with the secondary mouse button. Select the flag and request 1 explorer. Flags request units; they do not move them instantly. Explorers may stop to eat.

Construction consumes wood delivered by workers. Choose Inn from the building controls (the building palette), place it in clear ground near wheat, and request 2 builders. A worker target is a request, not a count of workers already present. Keep suppliers at your existing Inn and Swarm. Any valid location counts.

Construction and everyday supply have separate worker targets. Select the finished Inn and increase its operating target. A supplier gathers wheat and carries it here. Hungry globules eat at Inns; a building with no suppliers will eventually run out. Keep the wheat patch accessible.

The Swarm consumes wheat to produce units. Set worker production to 1 and explorer and warrior production to 0. Increase the Swarm worker target to 2 or more. More suppliers can deliver wheat faster, but they compete with other jobs. Maintain food supply at both Inns.

Open Flags, choose War Flag, and place it over the enemy Swarm east of the stone. Select the flag and request up to 4 warriors. A small radius keeps them concentrated. Leave placement with the secondary mouse button before selecting the flag. If no warriors remain, produce more at the Swarm. Warriors may stop to eat; keep the Inns supplied.
Your explorer needs an assigned Exploration Flag at the eastern stone patch. Check its target and explorer count.

If you removed the new Inn, build another. Otherwise check the construction site and its worker target. Existing supply jobs may occupy your workers; keep food running while making builders available.
Select the finished new Inn. Check its worker target and watch for wheat deliveries. Workers may need time to travel or eat.

Welcome to Globulation 2! This tutorial teaches colony management over four missions. You can save your progress from the game menu and load it later from the main menu. Press Space to continue, or tap OK on a touch screen. Some messages disappear after you continue; use Message history to read them again.
You begin with a Swarm and one worker. Let's see how they work together.
Your worker harvests wheat and carries it to the Swarm. The Swarm uses wheat to produce new units, making it essential to your colony.
Select your globule, the moving unit, with a left-click or a tap.
The unit information shows its food level falling over time. Your globule is getting hungry. When food bars are visible, the blue bar beneath the unit shows its remaining food.
Globules eat at Inns. Clear the selection with a right-click, or tap empty ground on a touch screen.

Open the building controls, choose Inn, and place it near wheat. Follow your worker's harvesting route if you cannot spot the wheat. On touch screens, use Build and confirm a valid placement. When finished, leave placement mode with a right-click or the touch Cancel control.
Good! The Inn's building site is in place.
A worker from the Swarm can now build the Inn. The worker gathers wood from nearby trees and brings it to the site. Wait for construction to finish.
The finished Inn needs wheat. An assigned worker will gather it, just as a worker supplies the Swarm.
The Inn's yellow resource bar rises as wheat arrives. It shows how much wheat the Inn has in stock.
Now let's learn how to assign work.
One worker supplies the Swarm and another supplies the Inn. Either may pause to eat at the Inn. That is normal.

Select the Swarm and find its worker assignment control. On desktop it is labeled Working; on touch screens, use the assigned workers and target control. The target is how many workers you want at this building.
Use the assignment control to set the Swarm's worker target to 0. Then select the Inn and set its target to 0 too.
Your workers are now idle, but they still need food. An Inn with no assigned workers will eventually run out of wheat.
A globule that cannot find food will lose health and may die. A Hospital can heal damaged globules, but you must also keep the Inns supplied.
Build a Hospital using the building controls. It does not need wheat, so place it near wood or in a central spot near your Swarm.
Select the Hospital's building site and set its worker target to 2. Two workers can finish it faster.
The Hospital is ready. Injured globules can now visit it to recover their health.
The black areas are unexplored. Units reveal nearby ground as they move. Workers follow their jobs, so they are hard to use for scouting. Explorers are designed for that task.
Select the Swarm and find the production ratios for workers, explorers, and warriors. Increase the explorer ratio to 1.
With worker and explorer ratios both at 1, the Swarm produces equal numbers of each over time. Set the worker ratio to 0 so it produces only explorers for now.
Set the Swarm's worker assignment target back to 1 so a worker can bring it wheat.
Select the Inn and set its worker target to 1 too. Your growing colony needs a steady food supply.
Now wait for the Swarm to produce an explorer.
Your explorer flies around the colony, revealing more ground. Let the Swarm produce a second explorer before continuing.
Select the Swarm again. Set the explorer production ratio to 0 and the worker ratio to 1 to resume producing workers.
There is stone east of your base. Remember this location; you will need stone later.
The trees south of the stone are orange trees. Select them to see their resource information. We will return to fruit later; for now, focus on the Swarm.
Set your Swarm to produce workers only: worker ratio 1, explorer and warrior ratios 0.
Let's grow the colony faster. Select the Swarm and set its worker assignment target to 6. You may not have six workers yet; new workers can fill the extra jobs as they become available.
We will start the next tasks when you have 8 workers. Keep the Swarm and Inn supplied while the population grows.
Several workers are now supplying the Swarm. More wheat deliveries mean it can produce units more quickly.
A new worker costs 5 wheat. Carrying wheat from a distant field takes time, so a Swarm often needs more suppliers than an Inn. Place food-dependent buildings near wheat when possible.
You now have at least 8 workers. Select the Swarm and reduce its worker assignment target to 1 to slow population growth while we build.
Your colony needs more feeding capacity. Build a second Inn north of the existing one.
Assign free workers to the new Inn's construction site. It needs only 3 wood, so more than 3 builders will not help much.
The finished Inn returns to its operating worker target, normally 1. Construction and everyday supply use separate assignment targets.
Workers can learn to move faster. A Racetrack provides that training.
Open the building controls and find Racetrack. On desktop, hover over its icon to inspect its description and cost. On touch screens, select it in Build to prepare placement. Do not place it yet.
A Racetrack needs plenty of wood and a little stone. Choose a central location so units can reach it easily.
Build a Racetrack, perhaps south of the Swarm. Leave clear space around it: training buildings need room to expand when upgraded.
Set the Racetrack construction site's worker target between 5 and 7. It needs 7 construction materials in total.
Once finished, a Racetrack trains visiting units without a continuing supply of construction materials or wheat.
Globules are entering the Racetrack to train. Once trained, they can run faster.
Select the Racetrack to inspect training progress. Its progress indicators show how close the units inside are to finishing.
Your trained workers travel faster and can deliver resources sooner. Keep watching food stocks as the colony grows; faster deliveries help only if enough Inns remain supplied.

Find the worker population counter in the HUD. The total shows your population; the available-worker figure helps you spot spare workers or unfilled jobs. Use free workers without assigning more jobs than the colony can support.
The HUD also shows explorer and warrior counts. Check these when planning production or assigning units to flags.
You have 2 Inns. Each basic Inn can feed 4 units at once, so together they have 8 feeding places. More than 8 units can become hungry, so leave enough capacity for queues.
Two Inns will not support a growing colony forever. Build extra feeding capacity before shortages turn into starvation.
Build 3 more Inns near wheat. Hungry workers stop working, and prolonged starvation kills them. Assign available workers to construction while keeping your existing food supply running.
Finish building 3 more Inns, bringing your total to 5.
The new Inns use their operating assignment targets after construction, normally 1 worker each. Check that they have suppliers and enough wheat.
The Racetrack has improved travel on land. Now let's teach the colony to swim.

A Swimming Pool teaches units to swim and needs wood to build. Place one in the large clearing northeast of the base, north of the stone. Leave space around it for upgrades and resource growth, and assign available workers to construction.

A Swimming Pool teaches units to swim and needs wood to build. Place one in the large clearing northeast of the base, north of the stone. Leave space around it for upgrades and resource growth, and assign available workers to construction.
The Swimming Pool is ready. Globules can now enter and learn to swim.
Select the Swimming Pool to inspect training progress. A basic Pool trains 2 globules at a time, just like a basic Racetrack.
Your trained globules can now swim. Soon we will give them a job that requires crossing water.
There is more to learn. If you need a break, save your progress from the game menu and return later.
Your colony has food and physical training. A School will teach workers the skills needed for better buildings.
A School improves workers' harvesting and construction skills. Building one requires algae, which grows in water. Your swimming workers can gather it.
Protect important training buildings. A School does not have to stand beside water; a sheltered inland location can keep it safer from attack.
Build a School in a protected spot, such as behind the Swimming Pool or southwest of the Swarm beside the Racetrack. Assign available workers to build it.

Select a building to see the workers assigned to it. On desktop, the configurable Toggle draw unit paths action can also show lines from units to their destinations; see Settings, Controls for its current shortcut. Wait for the School to finish.
Your colony now has Inns, a Hospital, a Racetrack, a Swimming Pool, and a School. It is time to prepare its defenses.
We have not produced any warriors yet. Without them, the colony has little protection against an attack.
Select the Swarm and set the warrior production ratio to 2. Leave the worker ratio at 1 so the colony keeps producing workers too.
The Swarm will now produce roughly 2 warriors for every worker. Assign more workers to supply it if you want faster production.
Your first warrior is ready and will begin training. Wait for a second warrior before continuing.
Warriors use the Racetrack and Swimming Pool too. They can also train their attack skills at Barracks.

Barracks improve attack strength and attack speed. Strength increases damage per hit; speed increases how often a warrior attacks. Well-trained warriors can defeat much larger groups of untrained enemies.
Build Barracks near wood, which is needed for construction.
Assign available workers to the Barracks building site. Keep enough workers on food supply and avoid creating more jobs than they can fill.
The Barracks are ready. Warriors can now train their attack skills there.
Our colony can grow stronger by upgrading its buildings.
Workers trained at the School can construct upgrades. Select an eligible building and look for Upgrade in its building controls. Damaged buildings may need Repair first.
Let's decide what to upgrade first. Our Inns still have spare capacity, so they can wait.
The Hospital also has room. We can focus on the School, Racetrack, Swimming Pool, or Barracks.
Upgrade the Racetrack first so units can learn to move even faster.
Select the Racetrack and choose Upgrade in its building controls. Units inside must leave before construction begins, so the change may not be immediate.
Assign available workers to the Racetrack upgrade. Only workers with the required School training can build a level 2 construction site.
Wait for the Racetrack upgrade to finish. Higher-level buildings take more resources and time to construct.
Your level 2 Racetrack is complete. It occupies more ground than before, which is why we left a gap. A building cannot upgrade without enough room to expand.
Now upgrade the Barracks and the Swimming Pool to level 2. We will continue when both are finished.
Upgraded buildings can generally serve more globules or offer better training. A level 2 Inn, for example, has 7 feeding places and feeds units faster than a basic Inn.
The enemy is nearby. Let's prepare for an attack.
Towers shoot at enemies within range. Walls help protect them. We will use both to defend a narrow approach to the colony.
Place towers in pairs if space allows. Walls can protect three sides, but leave a route open so workers can deliver stone ammunition.
Look east of the Swimming Pool, north of the other fruit trees. A narrow crossing leads toward another island. This is a good place to defend.
Plan room for 2 towers between the trees and the shore. Leave access behind them for stone deliveries and space on the other sides for walls. Do not wall the workers out.
Build 2 towers there. Assign 2 or 3 workers to each construction site, depending on how many are available in the HUD counters.
Use the building controls to place wall sections around the three outward-facing sides of the towers. Keep the side toward your colony open for workers.
Each wall section creates a construction job and needs 1 stone. If workers cannot fill every job at once, they can finish the sections in turn.
Wait for both towers and several wall sections to finish. The towers also need stone ammunition; the distant quarry makes deliveries slow. Increase their worker targets if you have spare workers.
Your colony has food, training, and defenses. Buildings can advance once more to level 3, providing stronger training and greater capacity. Keep improving them as resources and worker skills allow.
Look northwest of your base for the enemy colony. Move the view there now.
Explored ground can still be hidden by fog of war. To see the enemy's current activity, we need an explorer nearby.
Open Flags. This gives you flags and zones for directing units without controlling each globule individually.
Choose the Exploration Flag, shown with a kite-shaped symbol. Flags can be placed over land, water, resources, and unexplored ground.

Place an Exploration Flag over the suspected enemy base. An approximate location is enough to start scouting. Leave placement mode with a right-click, or finish the placement using the touch controls.

The outline around the flag shows its working radius. An assigned explorer will scout that area. Check your explorer count if none arrives, and produce another at the Swarm if needed. Press Space or tap OK once the explorer reaches the area.
The enemy has many workers and a gathered army. Let's prepare our defenses before it attacks.
Open Flags and choose the blue Guard zone. Use the mode for adding ground to the zone, rather than removing it. On touch screens, choose Paint rather than Erase.
Choose a brush shape and size. The large square is useful for painting a compact defensive area.

Paint a Guard zone just behind your towers, where the enemy is likely to approach. Click or tap to paint a spot, or drag to cover more ground. On touch screens, use Pan when you need to move the view while painting.
Available warriors will move into the Guard zone. Make it large enough for the defenders but small enough to keep them concentrated at the crossing. Now wait for the attack.
The enemy is approaching the crossing!
We are under attack. Watch how your trained warriors and towers defend the position.
You survived! Now open Flags and choose the spiked War Flag. Place it over the enemy Swarm to direct an attack there.
Leave placement mode and select the War Flag. Assign more than 1 warrior, then reduce its radius to concentrate the attack around the enemy Swarm. Wait for your warriors to arrive.
The attack has begun. Your warriors must get past the enemy towers to reach its Swarm.
Your warriors have reached the enemy base. Keep the attack focused on the Swarm.
You destroyed the enemy Swarm. Congratulations! You have completed the tutorial and learned the basics of food supply, assignments, training, upgrades, scouting, and combat.
